age.evidence: Male juvenile offspring were tested between PNDs 34 and 49.

sex.evidence: Male juvenile offspring were tested between PNDs 34 and 49.

dosing.evidence: Experiment 1: a single dose of either 1 or 3 mg/kg psilocybin... given intraperitoneally (i.p.) 8 days before behavioral testing... Experiment 2: repeated microdoses of psilocybin (0.1 mg/kg)... given i.p. three times every other day... Experiment 3: repeated microdoses of psilocybin (0.1 or 0.3 mg/kg)... given by oral gavage (per os, p.o.) three times every other day, for 2 consecutive weeks... Psilocybin... was dissolved in saline.

group_housing.evidence: On PND 21, the pups were weaned and housed in groups of three (same-sex and genotype).

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12/12 h light cycle with lights on at 07:00 h

assays.assay_description: Grey square arena (40 × 40 × 10 cm). Training trial: 5 min exploration of two identical objects. Test trial 30 min later: 5 min exploration of one familiar and one novel object. Measures: discrimination index, total sniffing time, line crossings (locomotion), rearings. Collapsed across three experiments with varying doses (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 mg/kg), routes (i.p., p.o.), and schedules (acute, repeated microdosing).

application_type.evidence: given intraperitoneally (i.p.)... given by oral gavage (per os, p.o.)

setup_restrain.evidence: each rat was individually placed into an open-field arena... and allowed to explore the objects

food_restriction.evidence: Short test in arena with no food present; ad libitum standard assumed but not explicit.

water_restriction.evidence: Short test in arena with no water present.

time_to_assay.evidence: Experiment 1: 8 days before behavioral testing; Experiments 2 & 3: behavioral testing starting 5 days after the last administration.

sample_size.evidence: Exp1: WT-VEH n=11; WT-PSY 1 n=10; WT-PSY 3 n=14; Fmr1-VEH n=13; Fmr1-PSY 1 n=13; Fmr1-PSY 3 n=14. Exp2: WT-VEH n=10; WT-PSY n=9; Fmr1-VEH n=9; Fmr1-PSY n=8. Exp3: WT-VEH n=9; WT-PSY 0.1 n=9; WT-PSY 0.3 n=9; Fmr1-VEH n=8; Fmr1-PSY 0.1 n=10; Fmr1-PSY 0.3 n=10.

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (1 mg/kg i.p., 8 days pre-test) partially mitigated the short-term NOR deficit in Fmr1Δ exon 8 rats, while 3 mg/kg impaired performance in WT controls. Repeated microdosing (0.1 mg/kg i.p., or 0.1–0.3 mg/kg p.o., every other day) fully normalized the discrimination deficit in Fmr1Δ rats without affecting WT animals. Total exploration time, line crossings, and rearings were unaffected by treatment.
outcomes.evidence: repeated intraperitoneal treatment with psilocybin microdoses normalized the short-term object recognition deficit displayed by Fmr1Δ exon 8 rats... repeated oral treatment with psilocybin microdoses normalized the short-term object recognition deficit displayed by Fmr1Δ exon 8 rats, without affecting the cognitive performance of WT animals.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single behavioural paradigm (short-term NOR); collapsed the three experiments (different doses/routes/schedules) into one assay per rubric rules.
